messages:
maria: Quick sync — HardwareCo reached out. They want their Edge‑TPU‑optimized open model distributed via AWS Marketplace + a co‑authored launch blog. Need to align on licensing, redistribution, and infra packaging. Who's in?

aj: +1 — happy to coordinate engineering / packaging. Do we have their exact license text? that’ll drive redistribution terms.

sasha: I reviewed the draft. It's a permissive non‑exclusive license but with a 'no re‑licensing' clause. Legal is flagged on redistribution of quantized weights. cc @legal-squad

legal-squad: Quick note: "no re‑licensing" is fine, but marketplace requires that we can redistribute a deployable artifact. We should get a narrow grant that explicitly allows redistribution to customers via marketplace listings and on‑prem images.

zach: From infra: packaging for Edge TPU will be a vendor artifact + Redwood adapter. Plan: ship two artifacts — (1) inference bundle with compiled kernels + metadata, (2) source model weights tarball with license pointer. Customers on Dedicated/Private get both; hosted API uses precompiled bundle only.

maria: That sounds sensible. For the listing we also need a compatibility matrix (chip versions), recommended quantization profiles, and an integrity checksum.

kevin: For SIs: we should prepare a 'deployment checklist' for partners that includes: network ports, accel drivers, benchmarking harness, and fallback model options. Can we include an "SI workshop" in the partner agreement?

maria: Yes — propose a 2‑day SI workshop + 30 days of onboarding support as part of the joint go‑to‑market. Marketing wants a co‑branded asset.

marketplace-bot: Listing draft created: hw-model-hc-edge-1850123456. Please add product docs and package URL.

aj: Engineering asks: need an artifact naming spec. Proposal: `hwco-edge-v{model_ver}-cpu/tpu-{quant_profile}.tar.gz` and a small manifest.json with fields: model_version, quant_profile, license_url, sha256. Example manifest snippet:
```json
{
  "model_version": "1.0.3",
  "quant_profile": "int8-edgetpv2",
  "license_url": "https://hardwareco.com/licenses/open-model-1.0.txt",
  "sha256": "..."
}
```

sasha: Legal: please ensure license_url points to an immutable permalink (tagged release) not a changing page. Also include an export control clause — some TPU binaries may be restricted.

legal-squad: Agreed. We'll ask for a signed addendum granting Redwood the right to redistribute the compiled bundle for customers in listed jurisdictions. Also request an indemnity carveout for modified forks.

zach: Ops note: hosted API can't accept binary TPU blobs. We'll host a compiled CPU fallback and redirect customers who bring their own TPU to the marketplace artifact. Need to mark the hosted endpoint as "TPU‑accelerated variant not available" in the product docs.

maria: Timeline check: HWCo wants a mid‑May announcement. Realistically we need engineering + legal signoff 2 weeks before that, plus marketing asset approvals. That puts our internal freeze in ~early May. Thoughts?

kevin: SI workshop can be scheduled in late April. That gives SIs time to integrate before announcement.

aj: Engineering estimate: 3 weeks to create packaging pipeline + CI to sign manifests and produce marketplace bundle. Need one fulltime eng and one infra SRE.

sasha: Legal estimate: 1 week to draft addendum if partner provides license permalink and confirms export control status.

maria: Ok — action items: (1) @aj spin up packaging PoC by next Tue, (2) @legal-squad draft redistribution addendum, (3) @kevin schedule SI workshop, (4) @zach add compatibility doc to listing draft. I'll coordinate with HWCo on permalinked license and co‑marketing assets.

marketplace-bot: Reminder: marketplace listings require a security scan of bundled binaries. Schedule a run with eng‑security before we submit.

aj: noted — I'll add a CI job that uploads signed artifact to a staging bucket for the scan.

maria: Perfect. One more: marketing asks we lock embargo date and speaking points by May 3 — I'll push back if they request earlier.

kevin: Also think about pricing/units: should we list it as "model license + infra" or purely a free model with paid support? HWCo prefers free model + paid support/consulting for SIs. Need confirmation for the marketplace SKU pricing structure.

sasha: Legal: free model + paid support is cleaner. We'll need an SLA for paid support if Redwood is on the hook for any managed offering.

maria: Good call. I'll ask HWCo to confirm the commercial model and send an updated MOU.

zach: I'll start the compatibility table template and drop it in the listing draft.

maria: Thanks all. If no surprises, we'll reconvene Thurs for a quick status update. :sparkles:
